Seminar Title:

Identification and investigation of signature microRNAs imparting chemoresistance in Oral Cancer: The miR-185-5p and miR-203a-3p/RRM2/RAN axis as a therapeutic target

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Life Science

Speaker Name:

Priyajit Biswal ( Rollno : 521ls2001)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

LS Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

12 Oct 2026 11.00 AM

Contact:

Bibekanand Mallick

Abstract:

Chemoresistance remains a major obstacle in the effective management of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Numerous studies have implicated microRNAs (miRNAs) in the chemoresistance of OSCC however, the exact molecular mechanisms underlying this process are still poorly understood. An integrative analysis of miRNA and gene expression profiles from drug-resistant OSCC cells identified a novel miRNA regulatory axis that regulates oncogenesis and chemoresistance in the malignancy.Furthermore, we identified novel pharmacological inhibitors that target key genes dysregulated by these miRNAs to overcome chemoresistance-related complications. Initially, we identified miR-185-5p as one of the signature miRNAs downregulated in chemoresistant OSCC cells, and its ectopic expression restored cisplatin sensitivity. In-depth investigation revealed that miR&ndash185&ndash5p upregulates miR-203a-3p via SOX9 suppression and sensitizes OSCC cells to cisplatin by decreasing key drug efflux and DNA damage regulators - ABCC1, ABCB1, RRM2, and RAN. Mechanistically, adaptive pro-survival signaling in response to chemotherapy is enhanced with cisplatin exposure through increased RRM2 expression and its RAN-dependent nuclear localization. We found miR-203a-3p disrupts this RAN&ndashRRM2 axis to restore cisplatin sensitivity. Hence, to overcome challenges associated with miRNA-based therapeutics, we identified KD-025 as a novel dual inhibitor targeting both RRM2 and RAN, substantially increasing cisplatin efficacy by inducing apoptosis and oxidative stress. These findings were further supported in 3D OSCC-derived spheroids. Together, our findings uncovered a previously unrecognized therapeutic vulnerability and propose KD-025 with cisplatin as a combinatorial therapeutic strategy to overcome chemoresistance in OSCC.
